destination.name: Dandenong Ranges
destination.tagline: Fern gullies, hill villages and a heritage steam railway east of Melbourne
destination.description: The Dandenong Ranges are low mountain ranges about 35 km east of Melbourne, rising to 633 m at Mount Dandenong, topped by a TV tower. Puffing Billy, a heritage steam railway, runs 24 km on its original mountain track from Belgrave to Gembrook and is the most popular attraction in the ranges. Sheltered gullies hold temperate rainforest, tree ferns and mountain ash forest, with superb lyrebirds and kookaburras. The ranges have been a day-trip and weekend retreat for Melburnians since the 1870s.
whyVisit: Ride a steam train through the hills
Walk fern gullies and tall forest

goodToKnow.title: Train from Melbourne
goodToKnow.detail: Belgrave line trains reach Belgrave in just over an hour, where Puffing Billy departs. Buses up the hills run rarely.

goodToKnow.title: Dress for the hills
goodToKnow.detail: Daytime temperatures run 4 to 6 C cooler than Melbourne's lower suburbs, and winter fog is common.

goodToKnow.title: Check fire restrictions
goodToKnow.detail: The ranges are bushfire-prone and summer fire restrictions apply. There is no camping in the national park and no rubbish bins.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Cooler, milder {months} weather suits walking, before summer fire restrictions and winter fog.
